p26.original: 5.6.1 短暂性：记忆消退导致遗忘
p26.en: 5.6.1 Shortness: memory loss leads to forgetting

p27.original: 在一项关于短暂性（transience）的经典研究中，心理学的先驱赫尔曼·艾宾浩斯（Ebbinghaus，1908，1973）第一次尝试学习一系列无意义的音节（如POV、KEB、FIC和RUZ），并在不同的时间间隔内对它们进行回忆。在短时间以至几天的间隔内，记忆效果还不错。但是在长达数周或数月的间隔后再测量记忆效果，艾宾浩斯已完全无法回忆起学习过的内容，他不得不发明另一个办法：通过记录自己重新学习原始列表所需的复述次数来测量自己的记忆水平。因为重新学习一个列表通常比最初学习该列表时所需的复述次数更少，所以这两种条件之间的差异意味着“节省量（或记忆存量）”，可以作为衡量记忆效果的指标。（如果最初学习需要10次，而重新学习需要7次，那么节省量是30%。）通过使用这种重学法（节省法），艾宾浩斯可以追踪到长时间间隔后的记忆。结合多次实验的数据艾宾浩斯得到了图5-11中的曲线，即艾宾浩斯遗忘曲线。它代表了艾宾浩斯最重要的发现：对于相对无意义的材料，我们在最初的遗忘速度会很快，但随后遗忘速度会逐渐减慢。随后的研究表明，这条遗忘曲线（forgetting curve）反映了我们的记忆存在短暂性模式，因此我们遗忘了所学的大量语言材料。
p27.en: In a classic study on transientity, Ebinghaus, 1973, the pioneer of psychology, tried for the first time to learn a series of meaningless syllables (e.g. POV, KEB, FIC and RUZ) and to remember them at different intervals. The memory works well between a short period and a few days. But to measure memory after weeks or months, Espinhos has become completely incapable of remembering what he has learned, and he has had to devise another way to measure his memory by recording the number of repetitions that he needs to retrace the original list. Since a list of relearning is usually less frequently repeated than is required for the initial study of the list, the difference between the two conditions means “savings” (or memory stocks) and can be used as an indicator of memory effects. (If initial learning requires 10 and re-learning 7 times, the savings would be 30 per cent. By using this re-engineering method (saving method), Ebinhos can track memory after long intervals. Combining the data from several experiments, Ebinghos received the curve in figure 5-11, the Ebinghos forgotten curve. It represents the most important discovery of Ebinhos: for material of relatively little significance, we forget at first speed, but then slowly at later. Subsequent studies show that this oblivion curve reflects the short-lived pattern of our memory, so we have forgotten the vast amount of language material we have learned.

p28.original: 图5-11 艾宾浩斯遗忘曲线

p29.original: 注：艾宾浩斯遗忘曲线表明，通过重新学习所反映的节省量会迅速下降到一个稳定水平，当节省量低于这个水平时，人们随时间流逝而遗忘的内容就不多了。
p29.en: Note: The Espinhos Forgotten Curve shows that savings reflected through relearning can rapidly decline to a stable level, and that when savings fall below this level, less is forgotten over time.

p30.original: 现代心理学家以艾宾浩斯的研究为基础进行探究，但他们更关注我们如何记住有意义的材料。例如，你如何记住在本书中读到的信息。有意义的记忆不会像艾宾浩斯的无意义音节那样迅速消退，这也是当你在学习概念时，应该用精细复述的方法来为概念赋予意义的另一个原因。你也可以在学习时运用艾宾浩斯的研究成果，即反复学习（或重新学习）可以帮助人们巩固记忆，防止记忆消退。
p30.en: Modern psychologists look at it on the basis of the Ebinhos study, but they are more concerned about how we remember meaningful material. For example, how do you remember what you read in this book? Meaningful memories do not fade as quickly as the meaningless syllable of Ebenhos, which is another reason why you should give meaning to the concept in a very elaborate way when you learn it. You can also use the results of the Eibenhos study in learning that repeated learning (or re-learning) can help people to consolidate their memories and prevent them from faded.

p31.original: 然而，并非所有的记忆都遵循经典的遗忘曲线。例如，我们一般会一直保持已熟练掌握的运动技能，即使不练习，也可以在程序性记忆中基本上完好地保持多年，“就像骑自行车一样”。我们对那些学过但很长时间没使用的外语的记忆似乎都能相对保持完好，甚至长达50年（比艾宾浩斯预测的遗忘水平要低）（Bahrick，1984）。类似地，即使长达45年以上，人们对高中同学的名字和面孔的再认准确率仍能保持在90%左右（尽管基于回忆的记忆任务显示人们保持的正确率要比这低得多）（Bahrick et al.，1975）。是什么使得人们对这些记忆的短暂性有所改善呢？我们将在这一学习阶段的最后对学习技巧的讨论中揭晓这个问题的答案。
p31.en: However, not all memories follow the classic oblivion curve. For example, we will generally maintain our skilled sports skills, which, if not practiced, can be largely preserved in the procedural memory for many years, “like riding a bicycle”. Our memories of foreign languages that have been taught but have not been used for a long time seem to have remained relatively good, even for 50 years (lower than the level of oblivion predicted by Ebenhos) (Bahrick, 1984). Similarly, even for more than 45 years, the re-recognition of the names and faces of high school classmates remains at around 90 per cent (although memory-based missions show that people maintain a much lower correct rate) (Bahrick et al., 1975). What has improved the shortness of these memories? We will find out the answer to this question at the end of this learning phase in the context of learning skills.

p32.original: 遗忘的生物基础 脑科学家最近发现了人们记忆消退的一个主要原因，并且这个原因可能会让你大吃一惊：记忆行为本身也会导致遗忘！是的，你没有看错，英国的记忆研究人员能够通过磁共振扫描真实地观察到这一过程。方法是这样的：他们首先教被试将一组词汇与图像进行配对，然后用这些词汇作为线索，让被试提取与每个词相关联的图像。每提取一次图像，被试对该图像的记忆就会变得更生动。这个模式可以通过与该记忆相关的神经放电体现出来。然而，与此同时，被试学过的其他图像会变得不那么生动，这表明当我们每次提取一个特定的记忆时，这一过程会主动抑制我们对其他竞争信息的记忆（Wimber et al.，2015）。
p32.en: The forgotten biological base, brain scientists have recently discovered one of the main reasons why people's memories fade away, and this may surprise you: memory behavior itself can lead to oblivion! Yes, you're not mistaken, and British memory researchers can actually observe the process through MRI scans. This is how they are taught to pair a set of words with images, and then use them as clues to extract images linked to each word. Every time an image is extracted, the memory of that image is tried to become more vivid. This pattern can be reflected in neurodeployed in connection with the memory. At the same time, however, other images tested become less vivid, indicating that when we extract a particular memory, the process proactively inhibits our memory of other competing information (Wimber et al., 2015).

p33.original: 这些发现在很多情况下都具有重要的意义。在警方调查和庭审的目击者证词中，目击者经常被反复询问事件的细节。我们现在知道，这个过程虽然会强化他们被问到的记忆，但同时也会抑制他们对事件中其他可能同样重要的细节的记忆。因此，随着时间的推移，他们的记忆可能会因为反复提取某些细节而变得扭曲，最终这可能会导致错误的判决。这项新研究还能帮助我们理解选择性记忆，甚至自我欺骗。
p33.en: These findings are of great importance in many cases. Witnesses were frequently repeatedly asked about the details of the incident in police investigations and witness statements at court hearings. We now know that this process, while reinforcing the memory of what they are asked about, at the same time inhibits their memory of other details that may be equally important in the event. As a result, over time, their memory may be distorted by the repeated extraction of certain details, which may eventually lead to erroneous judgements. This new study can also help us to understand selective memories, even self-deception.

p36.original: 干扰 造成记忆短暂性的另一个原因是干扰（interference），即一个事物不利于我们对另一个事物形成牢固的记忆。这种干扰经常发生在你尝试连续学习两个相互冲突的事物时。例如，你先上法语课，然后上西班牙语课。
p36.en: Another reason for the shortness of memory is interference, which is that one thing does not allow us to have a solid memory of another. This interference often happens when you try to learn two conflicting things over and over again. For example, you take French and then Spanish.

p37.original: 是什么导致了干扰呢？排在最前面的三个主要因素如下。
p37.en: What caused the disturbance? The three main factors that rank at the top are as follows.

p38.original: 1. 要学习的两套材料越相似，二者相互干扰的可能性就越大。因此，法语与西班牙语课程内容相互干扰的可能性比心理学与会计学课程相互干扰的可能性更大。
p38.en: 1. The more similar the two sets of materials to be studied, the more likely they are to interfere with each other. As a result, French and Spanish courses are more likely to interfere with each other than psychology and accounting.

p39.original: 2. 无意义材料比有意义材料更容易受到干扰。因为长时记忆是基于意义进行组织的，所以记住两个不同的密码比记住两个新闻故事更困难。不过你也可以利用这一点，通过让密码变得更有意义来更好地记住它们。
p39.en: 2. Unutilized material is more susceptible to interference than meaningful material. Since long-term memory was organized on the basis of meaning, it was more difficult to remember two different passwords than to remember two news stories. But you can also use that to better remember them by making them more meaningful.

p40.original: 3. 情绪性材料可能是引发干扰的特别强有力的来源。所以，如果你昨晚和你的真爱分手了，那么你可能就会忘记你的文学教授今天在课堂上说过的话。
p40.en: 3. Emotional material may be a particularly powerful source of disruption. So if you broke up with your true love last night, you might forget what your professor of literature said in class today.

p41.original: 对记忆的干扰有两种类型。
p41.en: There are two types of interference with memory.

p42.original: 1. 当原有的记忆扰乱了对新信息的学习和记忆时，就出现前摄抑制（proactive interference）。例如，每年的一月份我们都会受到前摄抑制的干扰，以至于无法写下正确的年份。当我们从一个计算机程序或应用软件切换到一个类似的新软件时，却一直试图用“旧的方式”做事；或者当新学期开始时，你发现自己正走向上学期上课的教室，这些情况的发生也是因为前摄抑制的影响。它也可能会导致你不小心用前任的名字称呼你现在的另一半！“前摄”意味着“向前”，所以在前摄抑制中，原有记忆会及时向前阻止你学习新的知识。
p42.en: 1. Proactive inhibition occurs when the original memory disrupts the learning and memory of new information. For example, in January of each year, we are affected by pre-suppression so that we cannot write the correct year. When we switch from a computer program or application to a similar new software, we keep trying to do things in an old way; Or when you start the new semester, you find yourself going to the classroom where you're going to school, and this happens because of the pre-scenes. It could also lead you to call your other half by the name of your predecessor! "Forecasting" means "forward," so in front-scenes, old memories stop you from learning new knowledge in time.

p43.original: 2. 当相反的情况发生时，即当新信息阻止了你对原有信息的记忆时，我们可以将这种遗忘归咎于倒摄抑制（retroactive interference）。“倒摄”的意思是“向后”，所以新的信息在进入你的记忆时，会向后将原有的信息挤出记忆（见图5-12）。
p43.en: 2. When the opposite happens, when new information prevents you from remembering the original information, we can attribute this oblivion to retroactive inhibition. “Rewinding” means “backward”, so when new information enters your memory, it squeezes the information back (see figure 5-12).

p45.original: 在计算机中，当你用新文档代替原有的文档时，就会发生倒摄抑制。同样的事情也会发生在你自己的记忆中。例如，当你在本章学到的新信息阻碍了你记起前几章的内容时，或者当你连续见到两个陌生人，第二个人的名字会导致你忘记了第一个人的名字时。

For example, when you learn new information in this chapter that prevents you from remembering the contents of the previous chapters, or when you see two strangers in succession, the name of the second person leads you to forget the name of the first person.

p48.en: Please provide examples of the memory errors that occurred as a result of the latest pre- and inverticulation interference. What kind of interference is it? How did it happen?

p49.original: 系列位置效应 你是否注意到一首诗或词语表的第一部分和最后一部分通常比中间部分更容易学习和记忆？通常，首因效应（primacy effect）是指对一系列项目中的第一个项目相对容易记忆的现象，而近因效应（recency effect）则是指对最近记忆的项目有记得更牢的现象。这两个效应加上对中间项目的记忆容易消退的现象，被统称为系列位置效应（serial position effect）。所以，当你被连续介绍和认识几个人的时候，你更可能记住最初和最后认识的人的名字，而不是在他们之间的其他人的名字。（这是假设其他因素相同的情况下，如名字的普遍性、外貌的独特性以及他们的性格。）
p49.en: Do you notice that the first and last parts of a poem or vocabulary are usually easier to learn and remember than the middle part? Typically, the primary effect is a phenomenon that is relatively easy to remember for the first in a series of projects, while the proximate effect is a phenomenon that is more firmly remembered for the most recent project. These two effects, combined with the loss of memory of intermediate items, are collectively referred to as the series of position effects. So when you are introduced and you know a few people in succession, you are more likely to remember the names of the people you first and last met, rather than the names of the others who are in their midst. (This assumes that other factors are the same, such as the universality of names, the uniqueness of their appearance and their character. I don't think so.

p50.original: 如何用干扰理论解释记忆的系列位置效应呢？与记忆诗歌或词语表末尾的材料不同，对中间部分的记忆会受到双重干扰，既受到前摄抑制的影响，又受到倒摄抑制的影响。也就是说，中间的材料会受到两个方向的干扰，而两端的材料只会受到一个方向的干扰。因此，考虑到系列位置效应的特点，也许特别关注本章中间部分的内容会对你的学习有所帮助。
p50.en: How do you explain the series of location effects of memory with the interference theory? Unlike material at the end of a memoir poem or vocabulary, the memory of the intermediate part is subject to double interference, both by front and back-suffocation. In other words, the intermediate material is subject to interference in two directions, while the material at both ends is subject to interference in only one direction. Therefore, given the characteristics of the series of location effects, it may be useful to learn from the contents of the middle part of this chapter with particular attention.

p51.original: 5.6.2 心不在焉：因注意不集中导致的遗忘
p51.en: 5.6.2 Ignorance: Forgetness due to lack of focus

p52.original: 当你找不到车钥匙或忘记了一个周年纪念日时，证明你曾经有过一段心不在焉（absent-mindedness）的时期，这是记忆的第二宗“罪”。这并不是说记忆已经从你的大脑回路中消失了。更确切地说，这是由于你将注意转移到其他地方导致的记忆提取失败。对于忘记周年纪念日这种情况来说，注意问题通常发生在提取阶段。当你把注意从即将到来的周年纪念日转移到其他事情上时，你就会忘记周年纪念日。至于找不到车钥匙，你的注意转移可能发生在最初的编码阶段，当时你并没有注意自己把钥匙放在了哪里。这种心不在焉的情况通常发生在边学习边听音乐、看电视或浏览社交媒体的时候。你可以通过图5-13中的实验来感受这种心不在焉的状态。
p52.en: When you can't find the car keys or forget a anniversary, it proves that you had a period of absence, which is the second “crime” of memory. It's not that memory has disappeared from your brain. More precisely, this is because of the failure of the memory extraction that you have caused by shifting your attention to other places. In the case of the forgotten anniversary, attention is often given to the withdrawal phase. When you turn your attention away from the upcoming anniversary, you forget the anniversary. As for the lack of keys to the car, your diversion may have occurred at the initial coding stage, when you did not notice where you had the keys. Such absence usually occurs when learning to listen to music, watch television or browse social media. You can feel this distracted state through the experiments in figure 5-13.

p54.original: 这种类型的编码错误也同样发生在加工深度实验中：对信息进行浅层编码的人（“该词是否包含字母e？”）比对信息进行深层编码的人（“它是动物吗？”）回忆目标词汇的能力更低。而另一个例子则是对于变化盲（change blindness）的研究：在一项研究中，被试观看了一段电影，其中一名演员正在问路，此时会有两名抬着门板的男性路过，他们的门板会暂时将问路的演员挡起来，在这个过程中，问路的演员会被另一名演员取代。令人惊讶的是，只有不到一半的被试注意到了这个变化（Simons & Levin，1998）。
p54.en: This type of coding error also occurred in the processing depth experiment: the person who encoded the information on a subsurface basis (“Is the word containing the letters e? “Is it an animal? The ability to remember the term "target" is even lower. Another example is the study of change blindness: in one study, a film was tested, one of the actors was asking directions, when two men with a doorboard would pass, and their doorboard would temporarily block the actors who asked for directions, and in the process the actors who asked for directions were replaced by another actor. Surprisingly, less than half of the people who have been tried have noticed this change (Simons & Levin, 1998).

p56.en: When are you going to be distracted?

p57.original: 在上面的实验中，你是否成了心不在焉“罪”的受害者？在什么情况下你最容易因为心不在焉而忘记某事？你能做些什么来克服它？
p57.en: Are you the victim of an uninvolved “crime” in an experiment on the subject? In what circumstances do you forget things because you're not in the mood? What can you do to overcome it?

p59.original: 阻断（blocking）是记忆的第三宗“罪”，当我们失去对信息的通达时，就会发生这种情况。例如，当你在新环境中看见熟悉的人，却记不起他们的名字时。然而，被研究得最彻底的阻断形式是令人抓狂的舌尖现象：你知道自己知道某个物品的名字，但却无法说出来。正如我们之前提到的，舌尖现象往往是由于个体缺乏背景线索（context cues）来激活必要的记忆图式而产生的。
p59.en: Blocking is the third “crime” of memory, which happens when we lose access to information. For example, when you see familiar people in a new environment, you cannot remember their names. However, the most thoroughly studied form of disruption is a gruesome tip of the tongue: you know the name of an object, but you cannot say it. As we have mentioned before, the tip of the tongue is often the result of the lack of background clues to activate the necessary memory pattern.

p60.original: 应激也会导致阻断，这可能是由于人在应激情境下无法保持注意焦点。同样，注意分散也会导致前瞻性记忆任务（如记住在特定时刻完成特定动作）受阻。年龄也在其中起到一定作用，随着年龄的增长，记忆阻断的频率也会增加。
p60.en: Stimulation can also lead to disruptions, possibly because people are unable to keep their focus focused in the context of passion. Similarly, attention to fragmentation can hinder forward-looking memory tasks, such as the completion of specific actions at a given time. Age also plays a role and the frequency of memory disruption increases as age increases.

p63.en: Explaining the crime of excessive conduct.

p64.original: 之前讨论的三种“罪”都是遗漏之罪，即以这样或那样的方式使记忆难以被提取。现在让我们把注意力转到过度作为之罪上，这是一种更主动的导致记忆提取失败的形式。
p64.en: The three “crimes” discussed earlier were all crimes of omission, i.e. in one way or another, making it difficult to extract memories. Let us now turn our attention to the crime of overrepresentation, a more proactive form that leads to memory extraction failure.

p65.original: 5.7.1 错误归因：错误背景下的记忆
p65.en: 5.7.1 Wrong attribution: memory in the wrong context

p66.original: 我们在提取记忆时可能会把它们与错误的时间、地点或人物联系在一起。沙克特（Schacter，1999）将此现象称为错误归因（misattribution），认为是长时记忆所具有的重构性质导致出现这一错误。这里有一个能很好地体现错误归因的例子：心理学家唐纳德·汤姆森（Donald Thomson）被指控强奸，依据是受害者对攻击者所做的详细描述（PsychBlog，2008）。然而，汤姆森有一个无可争辩的不在场证明：当犯罪发生时，他正在接受电视直播采访，而且采访内容正是关于记忆扭曲的知识！后来经调查表明，受害人在强奸发生前刚刚看了这期采访，并在应激经历下回忆起了汤姆森而不是袭击者的脸。这是一个典型的错误归因案例。
p66.en: When we extract memories, we may link them to the wrong time, place or person. Schachter, 1999 described the phenomenon as a misdirection, arguing that the reconstructive nature of long-term memory led to this error. Here is a good example of what is wrong: a psychologist, Donald Thomson, was charged with rape, based on the detailed description of the aggressor by the victim (PsychBlog, 2008). However, Thomson has an indisputable alibi: when the crime was committed, he was being interviewed live on television, and the content of the interview was knowledge of the distortion of memory! The investigation later revealed that the victim had just watched the interview before the rape and had recalled the face of Thomson rather than the assailant under stress. This is a typical case of error attribution.

p67.original: 并非所有错误归因的案例都如此戏剧化，事实上，大多数人几乎每天都可能犯这种记忆错误。例如，我们将自己在网上读到的一些内容认为是自己在课堂上学到的，或者我们以为自己从一个人那里听到了一些事情，实际上却是另一个人告诉我们的。错误归因还会促使人们误以为别人的想法就是自己的，从而导致无意识的剽窃行为。事实上，研究表明，这种情况发生的概率高达9%，即我们会无意识地把别人的想法当成自己的想法（Preston & Wegner，2007）。
p67.en: Not all cases of fault attribution are so dramatic, and in fact most people can make such memory errors almost every day. For example, some of what we read online is that we learned in class, or that we thought we heard something from one person, but actually another told us. Wrong attribution also leads to the mistaken belief that other people's ideas are their own, leading to unintentional larceny. In fact, studies show that this is a 9 per cent probability that we will unwittingly consider others' ideas as our own (Preston & Wegner, 2007).

p68.original: 然而，另一种错误归因会导致人们记住根本没有经历过的事情。研究人员让志愿者记住一组与特定主题相关的词汇：门、玻璃、窗格、阴影、壁架、窗台、房子、打开、窗帘、框架、风景、微风、窗框、屏风、百叶窗。在这种情况下，许多人后来记住了窗户这个词，尽管这个词并不在列表里（Roediger & McDermott，1995，2000）。这一结果再次表明了背景线索和图式在决定记忆内容方面的力量。它再次证明了人们会如何根据意义来形成和提取记忆。
p68.en: However, another wrong attribution leads to the memory of things that have never been experienced at all. Researchers remind volunteers of a set of terms related to specific topics: doors, glass, windows, shadows, walls, windows, houses, openings, curtains, frames, landscapes, breezes, window frames, screens, blinds. In this case, many later remembered the word window, although it was not included in the list (Roediger & McDermott, 1995, 2000). This outcome once again demonstrates the power of the background thread and the pattern in determining the content of memory. Once again, it demonstrates how people form and extract their memories according to their meaning.

p69.original: 5.7.2 易受暗示性：外部线索会扭曲或创造记忆
p69.en: 5.7.2 Vulnerability to suggestion: external leads distort or create memory

p70.original: 记忆也可以在暗示的力量下被扭曲乃至被创造，这是令庭审人员感到十分担忧的一项发现。律师或执法人员在询问目击者时可能就案件事实做出有意或无意的暗示，这可能会改变目击者的记忆。请思考下面的例子。
p70.en: Memory can also be distorted or even created by the force of suggestion, a finding that worries the court. The fact that lawyers or law enforcement officials may knowingly or unintentionally insinuate the facts of the case when questioning witnesses may change the memory of witnesses. Please think about the following examples.

p71.original: 当詹妮弗·汤普森（Jennifer Thompson）被强奸时，她镇定地将注意力集中在袭击她的人的身体特征上，这样如果她能幸存下来，她就可以对袭击者的样貌提供详细而准确的描述。
p71.en: When Jennifer Thompson was raped, she calmly focused on the physical characteristics of the person who attacked her, so that if she survived, she could provide a detailed and accurate description of the person who attacked.

p72.original: 詹妮弗·汤普森的记忆是正确的吗？在告诉你更多这个故事的内容之前，让我们来看看什么样的外部线索会影响记忆。记忆研究人员伊丽莎白·洛夫特斯（Elizabeth Loftus）和约翰·帕尔默（John Palmer）进行了一系列的研究，他们想检验目击者的记忆是否会因易受暗示性（suggestibility）而被扭曲。
p72.en: Is Jennifer Thompson's memory correct? Before I tell you more about this story, let's see what kind of external clues affect memory. Memory researchers Elizabeth Loftus and John Palmer have undertaken a series of studies to test whether the memory of witnesses is distorted by their vulnerability to insinuation.

p73.original: 记忆扭曲 在洛夫特斯和帕尔默的经典研究中，被试首先观看了一部关于两辆车相撞的电影，然后，实验人员要求他们估计汽车行驶的速度（Loftus，1979，1984；Loftus & Palmer，1973）。其中一半目击者被问的问题是“两车相互撞击时的车速有多快？”而另外一半人则被问的问题是“两车相互碰撞时的车速有多快？”结果发现，由于受“撞击”这个词的微妙影响，第一组估计汽车的行驶速度比第二组快了25%（见图5-14）。这种由错误信息引起的记忆扭曲被称为错误信息效应（misinformation effect）。对记忆的扭曲也可能受到另一种暗示的影响。在一个与之相关的实验中，一些目击者被问及一辆汽车经过谷仓时的速度有多快，而另一些人则被问道是否在视频中看到了谷仓。之后，被问及电影中是否有谷仓时，第一组被试更有可能会记得看到过谷仓（但实际上并没有谷仓）。这种类型的记忆扭曲，以及导致它形成的过程，显然对调查人员了解案件的真实过程造成了巨大的障碍。这些早期研究引领了更多研究来探讨记忆是如何通过类似的方法创造出来的。
p73.en: In a classic study by Lovetus and Palmer, they were first shown a film about two cars crashing, and then the experiment asked them to estimate the speed of the car moving (Loftus, 1979, 1984); Loftus & Palmer, 1973. The question that was asked by half of the witnesses was, "How fast did the two cars hit each other?" And the other half was asked, "How fast were the two cars crashing?" As a result, it was found that because of the subtle effects of the word “impact”, the first group estimated that the vehicle was moving 25 per cent faster than the second group (see figure 5-14). This memory distortion caused by erroneous information is referred to as the misinformation effect. The distortion of memory may also be affected by another hint. In a related experiment, some witnesses were asked how fast a car passed through the barn, while others were asked whether the barn was seen in the video. Subsequently, when asked if there was a barn in the film, the first group was more likely to remember seeing the barn (but not actually). This type of distortion of memory, and the process that led to it, clearly poses a huge obstacle to investigators' understanding of the true process of the case. These early studies have led to more research on how memory is created through similar methods.

p74.original: 图5-14 暗示对记忆的影响

p75.original: 注：在一项有关目击者记忆的研究中，研究人员通过改变询问被试的措辞来“暗示”不同的车速。那些暗示速度更快的词语会让被试对车速的估计更快。
p75.en: Note: In a study on eye-witness memory, researchers “indicated” different speeds by changing the wording of the interview. Those words that imply faster speed will make it easier to estimate the speed of the car.

p76.original: 编造的记忆 著名的发展心理学家让·皮亚杰（Piaget，1962）曾描述过他在童年早期经历的一个创伤性事件的生动记忆：
p76.en: The famous development psychologist Jean Piaget, 1962, described the vivid memory of a traumatic event he experienced in his early childhood:

p77.original: 如果我没有记错的话，我最早的记忆是在我2岁的时候，而且在15岁之前，我都相信自己清楚地记得下面所述的场景。我正坐在婴儿车里，保姆正推着它在巴黎的香榭丽舍大街上漫步，一名男子试图绑架我。我被带子固定在婴儿车上，而我的保姆则勇敢地挡在了我与绑匪之间。她的身上被绑匪划出许多伤痕，我现在还能隐约地看到她脸上的伤痕……
p77.en: If I remember correctly, my earliest memory was when I was 2 years old, and before I was 15 years old, I believed that I clearly remembered the scenes described below. I was sitting in the baby car, and the nanny was pushing it around on Champelishe Street in Paris, and a man tried to kidnap me. I was tied to a baby car, and my nanny was brave enough to stand between me and the kidnappers. She has many scars on her body drawn by the kidnappers, and I can now still see them on her face.

p78.original: 皮亚杰的保姆向其父母生动而详细地描述了这起所谓的袭击事件，并从他们那里得到了一块昂贵的手表作为对她英勇表现的感谢。然而多年以后，这个保姆给皮亚杰的家人写了一封信，承认自己编造了这个故事，并归还了那块手表。由此，皮亚杰（1962）总结道：
p78.en: Piage's nanny vividly and in detail described the so-called attack to her parents and received from them an expensive watch as a tribute to her heroic performance. However, years later, the nanny wrote a letter to Piage's family, admitting that he had invented the story and returned the watch. Thus, Piajje (1962) concludes:

p79.original: 因此，当我还是个孩子时，我一定听过这个让我父母深信不疑的故事，并以视觉记忆的形式投射到对过去的记忆中。
p79.en: So, when I was a child, I must have heard this story that convinced my parents and projected it into the memory of the past in the form of visual memories.

p80.original: 我们是否都很容易产生像皮亚杰故事中所描述的那种虚假的记忆呢？你觉得呢？
p80.en: Can we all easily produce false memories like those described in the Piajj story? What do you think?

p81.original: 为了找到答案，伊丽莎白·洛夫特斯和她的同事进行了一组新的实验。他们先联系了一些大学生的父母，并记录了这些学生童年曾经历过的事件。接下来，他们把事件列表给这些学生看，并询问他们是否记得这些事件。然而，学生们不知道的是，研究人员在那些事件列表中嵌入了一些看似合理，但从未发生过的事件。例如，在购物中心走丢了，在婚礼上打翻了酒杯，在迪士尼乐园遇到了兔八哥（这是不可能的事情，因为兔八哥不是迪士尼的角色），或者生日聚会上有小丑来访等（Loftus，2003a）。经过几天的反复回忆，大约有四分之一的学生都声称自己记得这些虚假的事件。而产生这一结果所需的只是一些可靠的暗示。（这个实验可能会让你想起本章开头提到的唐娜的案例：治疗师的反复暗示导致唐娜产生了虚假记忆。）
p81.en: In order to find answers, Elizabeth Lovetes and her colleagues conducted a new set of experiments. They first contacted the parents of a number of university students and recorded the events they had experienced during their childhood. Next, they listed the incidents to the students and asked if they remembered them. However, students are not aware of the fact that researchers have embedded seemingly reasonable but never occurring events in those lists. For example, he lost himself at the mall, ransacked the wine cup at the wedding, met the 8th Rabbit at Disneyland (which was impossible because he was not Disney's role) or had a clown visit at a birthday party (Loftus, 2003a). After several days of recollection, about a quarter of the students claimed to remember these false events. All that is needed to produce this result is reliable insinuations. (This experiment may remind you of Donna's case, which was mentioned at the beginning of this chapter: the repeated suggestion of the therapist led to Donna's false memory. I don't think so.

p82.original: 新的研究表明，伪造过的照片也会导致人们产生虚假记忆，而其效果可能比洛夫特斯和她的同事在实验中使用的虚假故事更甚。例如，在“购物中心走失法”的一个研究变式中，给成年人看一些伪造的照片，显示他们正在乘坐热气球。他们会在两周的时间里多次看这些照片，之后有一半被试会“记起”虚构的气球旅行的相关细节（Wade et al.，2002）。即使在这个数码相机和修图软件盛行的时代，人们也并不总是会停下来质疑一张照片是否是伪造的（Garry & Gerrie，2005）。
p82.en: New studies have shown that false photographs can also lead to false memories, which may be more effective than the false stories used by Lovetes and her colleagues in the experiment. For example, in a study variant of the “failure of shopping centres”, adults were shown false photographs showing them travelling in hot balloons. They will look at these photographs many times in two weeks, and half of them will be “remember” the details of the imaginary balloon trip (Wade et al., 2002). Even in this era of prevalence of digital camera and painting software, people do not always stop to question whether a photograph is forged (Garry & Gerrie, 2005).

p83.original: 影响目击者证词准确性的因素 那么，我们能在多大程度上依赖目击者的证词呢？显然，在实验室进行的实验有可能将虚假记忆从真实记忆中区别出来。但是在现实生活中呢？例如，我们在上文中简要提过的詹妮弗·汤普森，她是否能正确地辨认出袭击她的人？
p83.en: Factors affecting the accuracy of witness testimony, so how much can we rely on witness testimony? It is clear that experiments conducted in laboratories have the potential to distinguish false memories from real ones. But in real life? For example, Jennifer Thompson, who we have briefly mentioned above, can she correctly identify the person who attacked her?

p84.original: 詹妮弗·汤普森的案件，就像其他数百个案件一样，是由于错误但极其自信的目击者的证词导致的错误定罪。事实上，目击者的误认是错误定罪的主要原因，后来因DNA证据而被翻案的错误定罪案件中有超过75%是因此导致的。
p84.en: The case of Jennifer Thompson, like hundreds of other cases, was wrongly convicted as a result of the testimony of wrong but highly confident witnesses. In fact, the false identification of witnesses was the main reason for the wrongful conviction, which resulted in over 75 per cent of the cases subsequently reversed on the basis of DNA evidence.

p85.original: 如果有人宣称自己恢复了被长期遗忘事件的记忆，情况又会如何呢？正如我们在本章开头的第二个案例中提到的，罗斯的回忆在夏令营辅导员的忏悔中被证实，但人们并不一定能获得这种客观的证据。在没有客观证据支持的情况下，我们所能做的就是寻找可能会使人产生虚假记忆的暗示的证据，就像我们在错误记忆实验中看到的那种暗示一样。如果存在暗示，除非我们获得了客观的证据，否则对相关记忆进行适当的怀疑是必要的。具体而言，我们应该警惕目击者的报告受到以下几项因素的影响（Kassin，2001）：
p85.en: What would happen if someone claimed to have restored their memory of long forgotten events? As we mentioned in the second case at the beginning of this chapter, Ross' memories were confirmed in the repentance of summer camp counsellors, but such objective evidence was not always available. What we can do without objective evidence is to find evidence that could create false memories, as we saw in the false memory experiment. If there is an implication that, unless we have objective evidence, proper suspicion of the relevant memory is necessary. In particular, we should be wary of witnesses' reports being influenced by the following factors (Kassin, 2001):

p86.original: 诱导性问题（如“两辆车相互撞击时车速有多快？”）会影响目击者的记忆。但是，如果预先提醒目击者，询问会造成记忆偏差，那么诱导性问题的影响就会小一些。
p86.en: Inducing problems (e.g., "How fast are the two cars hitting each other?" It will affect the memory of the witnesses. However, if witnesses are warned in advance that questioning can cause memory bias, then the impact of induced problems will be smaller.

p87.original: 大量时间的流逝会导致原始记忆逐渐消退，使人们更有可能记错信息。
p87.en: The passage of a great deal of time can lead to a gradual erosion of the original memory and make people more likely to miss out on information.

p88.original: 重复提取：记忆每被提取一次，都会重构并被重新存储（就像提取、修改并保存计算机文档一样），这增加了记忆出错的可能。
p88.en: Duplicate extraction: Every time a memory is extracted, it is recreated and re-stored (like a computer document extracted, modified and saved), which increases the possibility of memory error.

p89.original: 目击者的年龄：幼儿和老年人尤其容易受到错误信息的影响。
p89.en: The age of witnesses: young children and older persons are particularly vulnerable to misinformation.

p90.original: 盲目自信：对记忆的信心并不能代表记忆的准确性。事实上，被误导的人的确会因为对方的自信而相信错误信息。
p90.en: Blind self-confidence: confidence in memory does not represent the accuracy of memory. Indeed, the misled do believe in the wrong message because of the confidence of the other side.

p91.original: 基于对上述因素的担忧，美国司法部（U.S. Department of Justice）发布了收集目击者证词的国家指导原则。
p91.en: Based on concerns about these factors, the United States Department of Justice (U.S. Department of Justice) issued national guidelines for the collection of eyewitness testimony.

p92.original: 5.7.3 偏差：信念、态度和观点会扭曲记忆
p92.en: 5.7.3 Distortions: beliefs, attitudes and views distort memory

p93.original: 沙克特将记忆的第六宗“罪”称为偏差（bias），指的是个人信念、态度和经历对记忆的影响。许多家庭对于“做什么”和“不做什么”的各种激烈争吵都可以归因于偏差。虽然看到别人的偏差比看到自己的更容易，但你也应该特别注意预防以下两种常见的偏差。
p93.en: Shaqt refers to the sixth crime of memory as a deviation (bias), referring to the impact of personal beliefs, attitudes and experiences on memory. Many families can be blamed for the bias in the various violent disputes over “doing what” and “doing nothing”. While it is easier to see others' deviations than to see yourself, you should also pay particular attention to preventing the following two common deviations.

p94.original: 期望偏差 期望偏差（expectancy bias）是一种无意识的倾向，即我们会更容易记住与自己的期望相一致的事件。例如，假设你是一名参加实验的志愿者。在实验中，你读到了一篇关于鲍勃和玛吉计划结婚的故事。故事中有一部分内容表明鲍勃不想要孩子，他很担心玛吉对此事的反应。当他把这个想法告诉玛吉的时候，她很震惊，因为她非常想要孩子。让人感到惊讶的是，在读了故事后你了解到鲍勃和玛吉最后结婚了，这一结果显然与你的预期相反。与此同时，另一组志愿者读了同样的故事，但被告知这对情侣最后分手了。除了结局以外，这两组人对鲍勃和玛吉故事的记忆会有所不同吗？
p94.en: Expectations deviations. Expectations deviations are an unconscious tendency to remember events that are consistent with our expectations. For example, assuming you're a volunteer in the experiment. In the experiment, you read a story about Bob and Maggie planning to get married. Part of the story shows Bob doesn't want kids, and he's worried about Maggie's reaction. She was shocked when he told Maggie about this idea because she wanted the baby so badly. Surprisingly, after reading the story, you learned that Bob and Marge were finally married, and that result was clearly contrary to your expectations. At the same time, another group of volunteers read the same story, but were told that the couple had finally broken up. Would the two groups have different memories of Bob and Marge's story than the ending?

p95.original: 在这个实验中，那些听到意外结局（即鲍勃和玛吉决定结婚）的人给出的错误报告最多。为什么会这样？因为他们的期望偏差，导致他们回忆出了被扭曲的信息，这些信息使结果符合他们最初的预期（Schacter，1999；Spiro，1980）。例如，有一个人“记得”鲍勃和玛吉已经分手，但后来他认为爱可以帮助他们克服彼此间的分歧，所以还是决定结婚。另一个人则记得，这对夫妇最终决定收养一个孩子以达成妥协。当某些事情与我们的期望不符时，我们可能会无意识中扭曲一些信息，使其更符合我们先前秉承的观念。
p95.en: In this experiment, those who heard the unexpected ending (i.e. Bob and Marge decided to marry) gave the most false reports. Why is that? Because their expectations were biased, they were reminded of distorted information that matched their original expectations (Schacter, 1999); Spiro, 1980. For example, one person “remembered” that Bob and Marge had broken up, but later he thought that love could help them overcome their differences and decided to get married. Another remembers that the couple eventually decided to adopt a child in order to reach a compromise. When something does not match our expectations, we may inadvertently distort some of the information to make it more in line with the ideas that we held earlier.

p96.original: 自我一致性偏差 人们讨厌前后矛盾的想法，尽管研究表明他们这是在自欺欺人。沙克特将其称为自我一致性偏差（self-consistency bias）。例如，研究发现人们对政治候选人的支持，以及对女性平权、帮助弱势群体等政治问题的支持，远没有他们意识到的那么前后一致（Levine，1997；Marcus，1986）。
p96.en: Self-conformity bias, people hate inconsistent ideas, even though research shows that they're deceiving themselves. Shaqt called it a self-conformity deviation (self-consistency bias). For example, the study found that support for political candidates and for political issues such as women's equal rights and support for vulnerable groups was far less consistent than they were aware (Levene, 1997); Marcus, 1986.

p97.original: 记忆研究对自我一致性偏差可以影响我们的记忆内容这一现象十分感兴趣（Levine & Safer，2002）。其中一项研究对情侣进行了相隔两个月的两次访谈，发现关于这段恋情的记忆会根据这两个月内恋情的进展情况而发生变化。然而，重要的是，被试通常没有意识到他们前后不一致。情侣关系改善了的那些被试所记得的自己对伴侣的最初评价比他们当初的实际评价要更积极，而关系恶化了的那些人则会有相反的反应（Scharfe & Bartholomew，1998）。通过这项研究以及其他许多涉及态度、信仰、观点或情绪的研究，我们可以看到偏差就像一面扭曲的镜子，我们的记忆通过这面镜子被反映出来，但我们并没有意识到我们的记忆已经被改变了。
p97.en: Memory research is very interested in the fact that self-conformity biases can affect our memory content (Levene & Safer, 2002). One of the studies, which interviewed couples two times in two months, found that the memory of the relationship changed in the light of the progress of the relationship during the two months. It is important, however, that they are often not aware of their inconsistencies. Those who have tried to improve their relationships have been more positive than their actual evaluation of partners at first, while those who have deteriorated will react the opposite (Scharfe & Bartholomew, 1998). Through this study and many other studies involving attitudes, beliefs, views or emotions, we can see deviations like a distorted mirror through which our memories are reflected, but we do not realize that our memories have been changed.

p99.original: 纠缠（persistence）是记忆的第七宗“罪”（见表5-2），它提醒我们，记忆有时过于有效。我们偶尔都会经历这种情况，一个持久的想法、一个图像或一段旋律会在我们的脑海中反复循环。值得庆幸的是，对大多数人来说，这种侵入性的记忆通常只是短暂的。然而，当这些记忆伴随着强烈的负面情绪时，它们就会成为问题。在极端情况下，对不愉快事件的记忆纠缠会导致情绪螺旋式下降，这也会使得抑郁症患者无法停止对生活中经历的不愉快事件或创伤事件的反刍思维。与抑郁症患者相似，恐怖症患者也可能会陷入对蛇、狗、人群、蜘蛛或闪电的可怕记忆中。创伤后应激障碍患者也可能无法抑制他们对创伤性经历的反复回忆。
p99.en: Persistence, the seventh crime of memory (see table 5-2), reminds us that memory is sometimes too effective. We sometimes go through this, and a long-lasting idea, an image or a melody recycles in our minds. Fortunately, for most people, this intrusive memory is usually only brief. However, when these memories are accompanied by strong negative sentiments, they become a problem. In extreme cases, the entanglement of memories of unpleasant events can lead to a downward spiral of emotions, which also prevents depression patients from putting an end to the reflexive thinking about the unpleasant events or traumatic events that they experience in life. Similar to depression patients, people suffering from terror can be trapped in terrible memories of snakes, dogs, crowds, spiders or lightning. Persons with post-traumatic stress disorder may also be unable to contain their repeated memories of traumatic experiences.

p101.original: 研究人员认为，一个被称为抑制控制的重要生理过程能够解释记忆纠缠形成的原因。就像当我们注意到一个正在掉下来的物体是一把锋利的小刀时，我们会抑制自己去抓住它一样，在正常情况下，当令人不安的记忆危害到我们的身心健康时，我们也会抑制这些记忆。然而，对于PTSD患者来说，这种类型的抑制控制受到了损害，从而导致他们的创伤性记忆会持续侵入。神经科学家认为前额皮层与海马之间存在的某种类型的沟通错误或功能缺陷是导致这种损害的生物基础。你可能还记得，前额皮层是我们大脑的执行器，它帮助我们制订计划、理性思考和解决问题。脑成像研究表明，PTSD患者的前额皮层的执行能力较弱，无法阻止海马提取创伤性记忆（Catarino et al.，2015）。
p101.en: Researchers believe that an important biological process known as inhibition of control can explain the causes of memory entanglement. Just as when we notice that an object falling is a sharp knife, we will restrain ourselves from catching it, and normally when disturbing memories endanger our physical and mental health. For PTSD patients, however, this type of inhibition control has been compromised, resulting in continuous intrusion of their traumatic memories. Neurologists consider some type of communication error or functional deficiency between the frontal cortex and the seahorses to be the biological basis for such damage. You may recall that the front cortex is the implementer of our brain, which helps us plan, think rationally and solve problems. A study of brain imaging shows that PTSD patients have a weak enforcement capacity for the front cortex to prevent the seahorse from extracting traumatic memories (Catarino et al., 2015).

p103.original: 丹尼尔·沙克特（1999）认为，尽管这“七宗罪”给我们带来了许多伤痛，但它们都源于记忆的适应性特征。
p103.en: Daniel Shaquet (1999) believes that, while this “seven crimes” have caused us many pains, they all stem from the adaptive characteristics of memory.

p104.original: 1. 因此，短暂性虽然使参加考试的学生感到恼火，但实际上它可以防止记忆系统被不再需要的信息所淹没。
p104.en: 1. Thus, while briefness irritates the students who sit the examination, it can in practice prevent memory systems from being flooded with information that is no longer required.

p105.original: 2. 同样，当阻断只允许最相关的信息——与当前线索关系最密切的信息——出现在脑海中时，记忆的阻断就是有用的。这一过程可以保护我们免受那些我们不需要的和会分散我们注意的记忆的侵袭。
p105.en: Similarly, when blocking only the most relevant information — the information most relevant to the current clue — is allowed to appear in the mind, it is useful to block memory. This process can protect us from memories that we do not need and that would distract us from.

p106.original: 3. 心不在焉也是我们转移注意这一非常有用的能力的副产品。
p106.en: 3. Ignorance is also a by-product of diverting attention from this very useful capability.

p107.original: 4. 同样，错误归因、偏差和易受暗示性也是由于我们的记忆系统只关注意义而忽略细节所导致的：否则就只能以牺牲意义为代价，让记忆系统像计算机那样存满信息。
p107.en: 4. Similarly, fault attribution, bias and susceptibility to suggestion result from the fact that our memory systems focus only on meaning and ignore details: otherwise, they will have to save their meaning to allow memory systems to be as full of information as computers.

p108.original: 5. 最后，我们可以发现，纠缠这宗“罪”实际上是记忆系统对情绪性经历（尤其是对那些涉及危险情况的经历）的一种反应性特征。因此，总体来说，记忆“失败”反映的是记忆系统为了更好地适应人们数千年来面临的各种情况采取的行动。
p108.en: Finally, we can find that entangling this “crime” is in fact a reactive feature of the memory system to emotional experiences, especially those involving dangerous situations. Thus, in general, memory “failure” reflects the actions of memory systems to better adapt to the circumstances that people have been facing for thousands of years.

p109.original: 5.8 运用记忆术来提高你的记忆能力
p109.en: 5.8 Use memory to improve your memory ability

p111.original: 描述记忆术如何帮助我们提高记忆力。
p111.en: It's like a little bit of a story about how memory can help us improve our memory.

p112.original: 提高记忆力的一种方法是自己在脑海中开发一套被称为记忆术（mnemonics，发音为niMON-ix，源自希腊语，意思是“记住”）的心理策略工具包。记忆策略（mnemonic strategy）通过将新信息与长时记忆中的信息联系起来，从而帮助你对新信息进行编码。为了进一步说明，我们将详细介绍两种记忆策略，即位置记忆法和自然语言中介，这两种方法对记忆各种清单特别有用。然后，我们会提供一些记忆技巧来帮助你解决如记名字等常见的问题。
p112.en: One way to improve memory is to develop a psychological strategy kit called mnemonics, pronunciated as nimon-ix, which comes from Greek and means “remember”. The mnemonic strategy helps you to encode new information by linking new information to long-term memory. For further clarification, we will elaborate on two memory strategies, namely, location memory and natural language intermediation, which are particularly useful for memory lists. And then we'll offer some memory skills to help you solve common problems like naming.

p114.original: 位置记忆法（method of loci，发音为LOW-sye，源自“轨迹”或“地点”）的起源可以追溯到古希腊时期，是本书提到的最古老的记忆方法。希腊的演讲家们最初发明位置记忆法来帮助他们记住演讲中的要点。
p114.en: The origin of location memory (method of loci, pronunciated as LOW-sye) can be traced back to ancient Greek times and is the oldest memory method mentioned in this book. Greek speakers initially invented place memory to help them remember the key points of the speech.

p115.original: 例如，想象一系列熟悉的地方，如你从家到学校的路上会经过的一些主要地标，然后使用位置记忆法在脑海中想象自己按照路线从一个地方移动到另一个地方，在移动的过程中把清单上的一个事物与其中一个地方对应。当你要从记忆中提取清单上的这些事物时，你只需再进行一次心理旅行，并检查你之前使用过的那些位置。在每个位置上，你都会“看到”你之前放在那里的事物。例如，如果你要记住购物清单，你可能会想象在你的房子上有一罐金枪鱼罐头，一瓶洗发水洒在了你上学时路过的溜冰场上，快餐店里放着一个碎鸡蛋等。奇异的或非常规的图像组合通常更容易被人记住。因此一罐金枪鱼罐头出现在你的房子上，会比它出现在超市里更让人印象深刻（Bower，1972）。显然，这种方法在很大程度上依赖于生动的表象，你的想象力越丰富，你就越能记住清单中的内容。你还需要对想象的路线和清单反复练习才能更好地掌握它——所以，对于购物清单来说，最好的方法还是把它写下来。然而，记忆比赛中的世界纪录保持者通常会使用这个策略，并能够很好地记住一长串名字、数字和卡片。从本质上讲，位置记忆法是一种赋予原本毫无意义的事物意义，从而提高记住它的能力的方法。
p115.en: For example, imagine a series of familiar places, such as some of the main landmarks on your way from home to school, and then use position memory to imagine in your mind that you move from one place to another along a route, matching one of the items on the list in the process of moving. When you're going to take these from your memory, you just have to make another psychological trip and check those positions you used before. In every position, you "see" what you put there before. For example, if you want to remember the shopping list, you might imagine a can of tuna in your house, a bottle of shampoo spilling over the ice-skating fields you passed in school, and a broken egg in a fast-food restaurant. A strange or unconventional image combination is usually easier to remember. So a can of tuna would be more impressive than it would be in a supermarket (Bower, 1972). Clearly, this approach relies heavily on vivid appearances, and the more imaginative your imagination is, the more you will remember what is on the list. You also need to practice the imaginary route and list over and over again to better understand it — so the best way to write it down is for the shopping list. However, world record-holders in memory games usually use this strategy and are well able to remember a long list of names, numbers and cards. In essence, locational memory is a way of giving meaning to something that is otherwise meaningless, thus enhancing the ability to remember it.

p117.original: 所谓自然语言中介（natural language mediator，NLM）的记忆术，是通过将新信息与有意义的词汇模式（如一个故事、一个首字母缩略词、一个韵脚或一首歌）建立联系来帮助我们记忆的。
p117.en: The memory technique of so-called natural language intermediaries (natural language media, NLM) helps us to remember by linking new information to meaningful vocabulary models (e.g. a story, a acronym, a rhyme or a song).

p118.original: 如果用这种方法来记住购物清单，那么你可以编一个故事。
p118.en: If you remember the shopping list in this way, you can make up a story.

p119.original: 还是使用与之前相同的购物清单（金枪鱼、洗发水和鸡蛋），为了将这些物品联系在一起，故事可以这样展开：“这只猫发现金枪鱼吃完了，所以它就在我用洗头发的时候打断我，并喵喵叫着催（egg me on）我买鱼。”（好吧，虽然我们知道这个故事是假的，但它的确能帮助我们记住这个清单！）
p119.en: Or the same shopping list (tuna, shampoo and eggs) that used to be used to connect these things, so the story could go like this: "This cat found that tuna was finished, so it interrupted me while I was washing my hair and screaming for me to buy fish. “Well, while we know the story is fake, it does help us remember the list! I don't think so.

p120.original: 同样，广告商也知道，使用押韵的口号和有节奏的音乐能让消费者更容易记住他们的产品和品牌名称。（现在你的脑海里可能就会浮现出一个广告的画面！）
p120.en: Similarly, advertisers know that the use of rhymed slogans and rhythmic music makes it easier for consumers to remember their product and brand names. "Now you're going to have an advertisement coming out of your head! I don't think so.

p121.original: 你以前的老师很有可能使用过简单押韵来帮助你记住拼写规则（“I在E之前，在C之后”）或每个月的天数（“九月有三十天”）。
p121.en: It is likely that your former teacher used a simple rhyme to help you remember spelling (“I before E, after C”) or the number of days a month (“30 days in September”).

p122.original: 在物理课上，你也可能用过以首字母缩略词的形式（用首字母组成的单词）出现的自然语言中介，来学习可见光颜色的正确顺序：如“Roy G. Biv”代表红色（Red）、橙色（Orange）、黄色（Yellow）、绿色（Green）、蓝色（Blue）、靛蓝色（Indigo）、紫色（Violet）。
p122.en: In physics, you may also learn the correct order of visible light colours by using natural language intermediaries in the form of initial abbreviations (words consisting of initials): such as Roy G. Biv for red (Red), Orange (Orange), Yellow (Yellow), Green (Green), Blue (Brue), Indigo (Indigo), Violet (Violet).

p124.original: 人们最常抱怨的记忆问题就是记不住别人的名字。那么，你要如何利用联想的力量来记住人名呢？首先你要知道，记住别人名字的过程不会自动发生。那些很快能记住他人名字的人通常会有意地把一个名字和这个人的某些特征联系起来，这种联系越不寻常，记忆就越深刻。
p124.en: The most frequent memory problem that people complain about is the inability to remember someone else's name. So how do you use the power of association to remember people's names? First, you know, the process of remembering someone else's name doesn't happen automatically. The more unusual the link between a name and some of the characteristics of that person is, the deeper the memory is.

p125.original: 例如，假设你刚刚在一个心理学大会上遇到了本书的作者。如果你想要记住我们的名字，你可以想象鲍勃（Bob）的脸被框在一个从他的名字中选取的大“O”里。要记住薇薇安（Vivian）的名字，你可以把她想成“活泼的薇薇安”（Vivacious Vivian），即大会上最活泼的人。至于菲尔（Phil），你可以想象把一根水管放进菲尔的嘴里并给他“灌”（fill）一点水。（尽管不寻常的联想可能比寻常的联想更容易记住一个人的名字，但最好不要告诉别人你想出了怎样的记忆术来记住他们的名字。）
p125.en: For example, assuming you just met the author of the book at a psychological conference. If you want to remember our names, you can imagine Bob's face being framed in a big "O" chosen from his name. Remember Vivian's name, you can think of her as the "Vivacious Vivian" -- the most popular person in the General Assembly. As for Phil, you can imagine putting a pipe in Phil's mouth and giving him a little water. (Although unusual association may be easier to remember a person's name than normal association, it would be better not to tell others what kind of memory you have in mind to remember their names. I don't think so.

p126.original: 总之，记忆术的使用让我们认识到记忆是灵活的、个人化的和富有创造性的。它还告诉我们，记忆始终会通过有意义的联想起作用。有了这些知识并亲自进行一些实验，你可以基于自己的个人联想，或许还有你的幽默感，设计出适合你的编码和提取技巧。
p126.en: In short, the use of memory makes us realize that memory is flexible, personal and creative. It also tells us that memory always works through meaningful association. With this knowledge and some experiments in person, you can design coding and extraction techniques that suit you, based on your personal connections and perhaps your sense of humor.

p127.original: 心理学很有用 运用心理学来学习心理学
p127.en: Psychology is useful. Use psychology to learn psychology.

p128.original: 那些为了记住名字或清单中一大堆无关项目而设计的记忆策略并不能帮助你在心理学课堂上学习。在心理学课堂上，重要的知识一般由概念组成，这些概念经常是抽象的，如“操作性条件反射”或“倒摄抑制”。你需要理解这些概念的含义，而不仅仅是记住它们。对这种材料的学习需要应用一些策略，这些策略既适合概念学习，又能避免大学生犯他们最怕的两宗记忆之“罪”：短暂性和阻断。让我们看看认知心理学家对那些想要避免自己犯这两宗“罪”的学生有什么建议。
p128.en: Memory strategies designed to remember names or a whole list of unrelated items do not help you learn in psychology classes. In psychology classes, important knowledge is generally composed of concepts, which are often abstract, such as “operational refraction” or “reverse inhibition”. You need to understand what these concepts mean, not just remember them. Learning about this material requires the application of strategies that are both conceptually appropriate and avoid the “crime” of two of their worst memories: transientness and disruption. Let's see what cognitive psychologists suggest to students who want to avoid committing these two “crimes”.

p129.original: 学习避免记忆的短暂性
p129.en: Learning to avoid the shortness of memory

p130.original: 为需要学习的材料赋予个人化的意义。许多研究都揭示了精细复述的作用，当记忆是有意义的而不只是事实和定义的集合时，我们的记忆会更牢固（Baddeley，1998；Haberlandt，1999）。所以，如果你能主动为一个新概念想出个人化的案例，或者在概念之间建立联系，你就会为这些材料建立一个更强的提取线索。你也可以使用整体记忆法（whole method）来加强记忆，需要在短时间内记住剧本内容的演员经常使用这个方法。在使用这种方法时，你要对所有的材料进行概述，从而形成“全局”，并能将细节融入其中。假如你们下周要考这一章的内容，当你使用整体记忆法时，你首先要通读本章的大纲和摘要，以及所有的标题和副标题，然后再开始阅读本章的细节内容。你也可以经常查看章节目录，用来提醒自己思考如何将正在学习的概念融入本章的大背景中。这种方法帮助你建立了一个心理框架，你可以在这个框架上填入编码、干扰、提取和其他记忆主题的细节。
p130.en: Personalized content is given to materials that need to be studied. Many studies have revealed the role of precision, and our memories will be stronger when they are meaningful and not just a collection of facts and definitions (Baddeley, 1998); Haberlandt, 1999. So, if you can come up with personalized cases for a new concept or establish links between concepts, you can create a stronger extraction trail for these materials. You can also use the whole memory method, which is often used by actors who need to remember the content of the script in a short time. In using this method, you need to summarize all the material, so that it can be “global” and incorporate the details. If you are going to take the chapter's contents next week, when you use the whole memory method, you will first read the outline and summary of this chapter, as well as all the headings and subheadings, and then start reading the details of this chapter. You can also look frequently at the catalogue of chapters to remind yourself of how to integrate the concept of learning into the broader context of this chapter. This approach helps you to create a psychological framework on which you can enter details of coding, jamming, extraction and other memory themes.

p131.original: 将学习内容分散到不同时间学习。接下来，你可以使用分散学习（distributed learning）的方法来抵抗记忆的短暂性。换句话说，你应该反复、频繁地间隔学习心理学知识，而不是期望通过一次性的“填鸭”来记住相关内容［这种方法被称为集中学习（massed learning）］。分散学习不仅避免了因集中学习的疲劳导致的学习效率低下的问题，而且还能在巩固过程中强化对知识的记忆。并且，每次你在学习时，都会复习已经学过的内容，并利用重复曝光（repeated exposure）的力量来帮助你巩固自己的记忆。一项研究发现，相比那些只用一个时段学习的学生，将知识分两个独立时段学习的学生，在同样的时间长度内，不仅能够记住两倍的知识，而且还能更好地理解学习的内容（Bahrick et al.，1993）。分散学习也会使学习材料保持得更久（Schmidt & Bjork，1992）。这种方法还有助于理解为什么几十年后我们仍能很好地记住读高中时朋友的名字和面孔：这很可能是因为我们在高中时频繁地提取这些信息，这相当于进行了分散学习。
p131.en: The content of learning is spread over time. And then you can use the dispersed learning method to resist the shortness of memory. In other words, you should learn about psychology repeatedly and frequently, rather than expect to remember the content through a one-time “ducking”. [This method is called focused learning]. Decentralized learning not only avoids the inefficiencies of learning caused by fatigue in concentrated learning, but also strengthens the memory of knowledge during consolidation. And every time you study, you study what you have learned and use the power of repeated exposure to help you consolidate your memory. One study found that students who study in two separate periods of time in comparison to those who study in only one period of time are able to remember not only twice the amount of knowledge but also a better understanding of the content of their studies within the same length of time (Bahrick et al., 1993). Decentralized learning also keeps learning materials longer (Schmidt & Bjork, 1992). This approach also helps to understand why, decades later, we still remember well the names and faces of our friends in high school: it is probably because we often extract this information in high school, which amounts to a decentralization of learning.

p132.original: 采取积极措施尽量减少干扰。虽然你不能完全避开对记忆的干扰因素，但你可以避免在为明天的心理考试复习完后再学习另一门课的知识。你还可以找出那些你容易混淆、彼此相似的概念或术语，并额外花时间区分它们的差异。
p132.en: Take positive measures to minimize interference. While you cannot completely avoid interference with memory, you can avoid learning about another subject after a review for tomorrow's psychological exam. You can also identify concepts or terms that are easily confused and similar, and take extra time to distinguish between them.

p133.original: 学习避免在考试时出现记忆阻断
p133.en: Learning to avoid memory disruptions during exams

p134.original: 上面提到的策略能帮助你在考试前对需要掌握的知识形成牢固的记忆。不过，要想在考试中取得好成绩，你还必须避免记忆阻断，即无法提取记忆中的内容的现象。为了帮助你做到这一点，我们建议你应用一些技巧，这些技巧会用到你在本章中学到的两个概念，即精细复述和编码特异性。
p134.en: The strategies mentioned above can help you to develop a solid memory of the knowledge you need to know before the exams. However, in order to achieve good results in the examination, you must also avoid the phenomenon of memory interruption, i.e., the inability to extract the contents of the memory. In order to help you do this, we suggest that you apply techniques that will be used in the two concepts that you have learned in this chapter, namely, precision recapitulation and coding specificity.

p135.original: 复习需要记忆的材料。学生们通常认为他们只需要读一遍材料并理解它们，这样就能够记住它们。然而，对于那些复杂的概念和观点，你要经过多次的复习才能记住它们。并且你在复习时不应该是盲目和被动的，如仅仅看看书中的内容。相反，你需要主动地进行复习，你可以用标题、副标题和关键词来测验自己，确定你准确记住了多少内容。考试能否获得成功的一部分原因在于，你能以多快的速度提取所需的知识。所以，你要记住，每次你在学习时提取了相关内容的记忆，你回忆它们的速度就能得到提高。而且，每次你都可以从不同的地方开始复习，这样你就可以利用系列位置效应加强自己的记忆。
p135.en: The study requires memory materials. Students usually think they need to read and understand them, so they can remember them. However, those complex concepts and perspectives will have to be reviewed several times before they can be remembered. And you shouldn't be blind and passive in your study, just looking at what's in the book. Instead, you need to take the initiative to review, and you can test yourself with titles, subtitles and keywords to determine exactly how much you remember. Part of the reason for the success of the examination is how quickly you can extract the knowledge required. So, remember, every time you learn to take a memory of what you're learning, the speed of remembering them can be increased. And every time you can go from place to place, you can use the series of location effects to strengthen your memory.

p136.original: 用你认为在考试中会出现的提取线索来测试自己。通过编码特异性原则，你就能以考试中最有可能出现的提问方式来复习。与一个在准备相同考试的朋友一起做这件事通常会更容易，最佳时机是在考试的前几天，在你已经完成复习、感觉自己已经准备好了的时候。此时你的目标不是学习新的材料，而是练习你已经学过的且你预测最可能出现在考试中的知识。这门课的教授喜欢出论述题、简答题或是选择题？试着思考并回答考试中最有可能出现的问题。
p136.en: Test yourself with what you think will happen in the exam. By the principle of coding, you can revisit it by the most likely question-and-answer method in the examination. It is usually easier to do this with a friend who is preparing the same test, the best time being just a few days before the examination, when you have finished your study and feel that you are ready. Your goal at this point is not to learn new materials, but to practice knowledge that you have learned and that you predict is most likely to appear in the examination. Are the professors in this class interested in talking, answering or choosing? Try to think and answer the most likely questions in the examination.

p137.original: 所有这些学习策略都是建立在已经确立的学习和记忆原则的基础上。以这种方式进行学习看起来可能需要完成很多工作，虽然事实的确是这样，但最终收获的成果却值得我们为之努力。
p137.en: All these learning strategies are based on established learning and memory principles. Learning in this way seems likely to require a lot of work, and while it is true that this is the case, the results of the final harvest are worth our efforts.

p138.original: 批判性思维的应用：对“恢复的记忆”的争论
p138.en: Application of critical thinking: debate on “restoration memory”

p139.original: 现在让我们将注意转回到本章开始时提到的两个案例。这两个案例都涉及当事人宣称其恢复了一段记忆：罗斯对自己被营地辅导员骚扰的记忆是准确的，而唐娜对父亲虐待自己的记忆则最终被判断是错误的。那么，当我们听到其他类似恢复记忆的说法时，我们该怎么办呢？
p139.en: Let us now turn our attention to the two cases mentioned at the beginning of this chapter. In both cases, the persons concerned claimed that they had recovered a memory: Ross ' memory of his harassment by camp counsellors was accurate, while Donna's memory of her father's abuse was ultimately judged wrong. So, what do we do when we hear other similar stories about the restoration of memory?

p141.original: 争论的焦点是恢复的记忆的准确性，而不是性虐待之类事件的真实性。恢复的记忆是否是虚假的？如果有可能，那么我们就必须去判断它们的准确性，尤其是关于创伤性事件的记忆。
p141.en: The debate focused on the accuracy of the memory of recovery rather than on the truth of events such as sexual abuse. Is the memory of recovery a false one? If possible, then we must judge their accuracy, especially with regard to the memory of traumatic events.

p142.original: 恢复记忆的观点是合理的还是极端的？
p142.en: Is the idea of restoring memory reasonable or extreme?

p143.original: 让我们从这个问题开始讨论：有关性虐待的记忆恢复这件事是合理的还是离谱的？也就是说，它是否符合我们对记忆和性虐待所知的事实？让我们看看下面的证据能告诉我们什么。
p143.en: Let us start with this: is it reasonable or irrational to remember sexual abuse? In other words, is it consistent with the fact that we know about memory and sexual abuse? Let's see what the evidence below tells us.

p144.original: 需要强调的是，确实存在儿童遭到性虐待的事件，这也构成了严重的社会问题。这有多普遍呢？虽然不同的估计之间相差很大，但在美国大约有4%到20%的儿童至少经历过一次性虐待（McAnulty & Burnette，2004；Terry & Tallon，2004）。当然，我们很难获得准确的数据，因为人们可能不愿意说起这些经历。而且，如果性虐待的记忆真的可以长时间被屏蔽在意识之外，那么实际的数字可能就会更高。
p144.en: It should be stressed that there are cases of sexual abuse of children, which also constitutes a serious social problem. How common is this? Although the estimates vary widely, about 4 to 20 per cent of children in the United States have experienced sexual abuse at least once (McAnulty & Burnette, 2004); Terry & Tallon, 2004. Of course, it is very difficult to obtain accurate data, as people may be reluctant to speak of those experiences. Moreover, if the memory of sexual abuse can really be kept away from consciousness for a long time, then the actual figures may be higher.

p145.original: 我们还应该注意到，大多数声称遭到性虐待的人并不存在“恢复的”记忆。总之，我们没有理由去怀疑那些说自己被性骚扰过并一直铭记在心的人。争论的焦点在于一小部分记忆被遗忘数月甚至数年之后突然“被恢复”。
p145.en: We should also note that the majority of those who claim to have been sexually abused do not have a “recovered” memory. In any case, there is no reason to question those who say they have been sexually harassed and who have been kept in mind. The debate focused on the fact that a small part of the memory was forgotten for months or even years and suddenly “recovered”.

p147.original: 公众怀有一种强烈但毫无根据的信念，即认为人们对创伤事件最常见的反应是压抑，正如西格蒙德·弗洛伊德最早提出的那样。但是，事实上，大多数有创伤性经历的人并不会忘记这段记忆，而是对它们历历在目（McNally et al.，2003）。对那些令人不安的经历的不愉快回忆正是创伤后应激障碍的问题所在。那么，我们如何解释以下事实，即在这一领域的几乎每一项研究中都有一部分案例会报告其存在压抑的现象（Greenhoot et al.，2008）？
p147.en: The public has a strong but unfounded belief that the most common reaction to traumatic events is depression, as Siegmond Freud first suggested. In fact, however, most people with traumatic experiences do not forget this memory, but rather are aware of it (McNally et al., 2003). The unfortunate memories of those disturbing experiences are precisely the problem of post-traumatic stress disorder. How, then, can we explain the fact that in almost every study in this field, a part of the case will report the existence of depression (Greenhoot et al., 2008)?

p148.original: 直到最近，心理学家们还无法回答这个问题。但现在，加利福尼亚州立大学的心理学家盖尔·古德曼及其同事（Goodman et al.，2010）可能已经找到了答案。他们的一系列研究表明，回避型依恋（avoidant attachment style）的儿童——或者那些对环境及其中主要人物缺乏信任的儿童在虐待事件发生时不太可能对该事件进行心理加工，这使得记忆被编码并被存储在长时记忆中的可能性降低。对这些个体来说，面对创伤事件的最终结果可能确实会形成被称为“压抑”的反应。
p148.en: Until recently, psychologists were unable to answer the question. But now, Geor Goodman et al., a psychologist at California State University, and his colleagues, may have found the answer. A series of their studies have shown that children who avoid attachments - or those who lack trust in the environment and its principals - are less likely to undergo psychological processing of the abuse at the time of the abuse, which reduces the likelihood that memories will be coded and stored in long-term memory. For these individuals, the end result of the traumatic event may indeed be a reaction known as “pressure”.

p149.original: 相关结论是否存在被偏差污染的可能？
p149.en: Is there a risk of contamination by deviation?

p150.original: 我们已经知道，记忆并不能完整地记录我们的经历。我们对经历的记录也并不总是准确的。与恢复记忆之争尤为相关的是一项我们在本章中讨论过的研究，它揭示了记忆很容易因暗示被修改甚至捏造。结果显示，被试不仅会报告虚假记忆，而且会相信它们是真实发生的（Bruck & Ceci，2004）。这类实验应该会让我们怀疑在治疗或审讯过程中使用暗示性技术所恢复的记忆。记忆专家伊丽莎白·洛夫特斯认为，那些假定大多数心理问题都源于儿童期性虐待经历的治疗师的确会使用暗示性技术，尽管她没有说明这个问题可能有多普遍（Loftus，2003a，2003b）。在《制造怪物》（Making Monsters）一书中，社会心理学家理查德·奥夫舍（Richard Ofshe）和他的合著者描述了来访者如何在不知情的情况下调整他们的回忆以符合治疗师的期望。他还补充说：“治疗师经常会鼓励来访者基于新的虚假记忆重新定义他们的生活历史，以及他们对家庭和自己最基本的认识。”（Ofshe & Watters，1994，p.6）
p150.en: As we already know, memory does not provide a complete record of our experiences. Our record of experience is also not always accurate. Of particular relevance to the struggle for the restoration of memory is a study that we have discussed in this chapter, which reveals the ease with which memory can be modified or even fabricated by implication. The results show that they not only report false memories but also believe that they are real (Bruck & Ceci, 2004). Such experiments should cast doubt on the memory restored by the use of implied technologies during treatment or interrogation. The memory specialist Elizabeth Lovetes argued that the therapists who assumed that most of the psychological problems originated from the experiences of child sexual abuse did use implied techniques, although she did not explain how widespread the problem might be (Loftus, 2003a, 2003b). In the book Make Monsters, the social psychologist Richard Ofshe and his co-author described how visitors were unknowingly adapting their memories to the expectations of the therapist. He added: “The therapists often encourage visitors to redefine their life history based on new false memories and their most basic knowledge of the family and themselves. ) (Ofshe & Watters, 1994, p. 6)

p151.original: 我们并不是说所有或者大多数治疗师都会使用暗示性的技术来探寻来访者遭受性虐待的记忆，尽管有一些确实如此（Poole et al.，1995）。然而，对于那些使用催眠、梦境分析和暗示性提问等技术来“钓”被压抑的早期性经历记忆的治疗师，来访者还是应该提高警惕。目前没有证据表明这些方法能够帮助我们恢复准确的记忆。
p151.en: We do not say that all or most therapists use implicit techniques to find out about the sexual abuse of visitors, although some do (Poole et al., 1995). However, visitors should be more vigilant towards therapists who use techniques such as hypnosis, dream analysis and implied questions to “fish” the repressed early sexual memory. There is currently no evidence that these methods will help us to restore accurate memory.

p152.original: 另一个暗示性来源是《治愈的勇气》（The Courage to Heal）一书，该书导致了大量令人震惊的恢复记忆案例的出现。这本书认为，被遗忘的乱伦和虐待记忆可能是人们感到无力、缺乏自信、脆弱和其他一系列不愉快的想法和情绪背后的原因（Bass & Davis，1988）。作者在书中写道：“如果你……觉得自己曾经遭受过虐待，那么它很可能发生过。”但是，这些断言只不过是推测。因此，记忆专家伊丽莎白·洛夫特斯和凯瑟琳·凯查姆（Katherine Ketcham）表示（1994），《治愈的勇气》可能导致了许多关于性虐待的虚假记忆的产生。
p152.en: Another implied source is The Courage to Health, which has led to a large number of alarming cases of memory restoration. The book argues that forgotten memories of incest and abuse may be behind people's feeling of weakness, lack of self-confidence, vulnerability and a range of other unpleasant thoughts and emotions (Bass & Davis, 1988). The author wrote: “If you feel that you have been abused, then it is likely to happen. However, these assertions are mere speculation. Thus, memory specialists Elizabeth Lovetes and Katherine Ketchham have stated (1994) that " Courage for healing " could lead to many false memories of sexual abuse.

p153.original: 我们还应该注意到，恢复的记忆这个问题既复杂又充满了情绪因素，在这种情况下很容易产生情绪偏差。性虐待问题不仅会破坏许多人与家庭的关系，而且我们也不会对那些认为自己是性虐待受害者的人置之不理。然而，我们对记忆的认识告诉我们，在没有确凿证据的情况下，我们不应该认为那遗忘已久的创伤性记忆真实发生过。
p153.en: We should also note that the issue of restored memory is complex and emotional, and in such cases it can easily lead to emotional deviations. Not only will the problem of sexual abuse undermine many relationships with families, but we will not ignore those who consider themselves victims of sexual abuse. However, our perception of memory tells us that, in the absence of conclusive evidence, we should not consider that long-lost traumatic memory to have actually occurred.

p154.original: 理性是否避免了常见谬误？

p155.original: 当观察事物之间的联系时，我们有一种自然的倾向，即猜想其中一个可能会导致另一个。例如，我们会把暴饮暴食与体重增加联系在一起，或者把长时间暴露在太阳下与晒伤联系在一起。在大多数时候，这种逻辑对我们很有帮助，但它偶尔也会导致我们得出错误的结论。例如，我们认为打冷战会导致感冒，或吃甜食会导致“糖兴奋效应”。专家们将这种现象称为事后归因谬误：事后的字面意思是“在事实发生之后”，事后归因谬误是指当我们回顾连续发生的事件（如吃糖之后兴奋）时，我们可能会错误地认为第一件事是第二件事的原因。
p155.en: When we look at the links between things, we have a natural tendency to assume that one of them could lead to the other. For example, we will link heavy consumption with weight gain or long-term exposure to the sun and sunburn. This logic has been very helpful to us most of the time, but it has occasionally led us to the wrong conclusion. We believe, for example, that fighting the cold war can lead to cold or sugar can lead to “sugar stimuli”. The experts described this phenomenon as a fallacy: it literally means “after the fact” and a fallacy means that when we look back at successive events (e.g. when we are excavated by sugar), we may mistakenly think that the first thing is the reason for the second.

p156.original: 事后归因谬误对“恢复的记忆”的争论有何贡献？当人们“回顾”他们的记忆，并发现自己被虐待的记忆（不知准确与否）似乎与他们当前的不快乐有关时，他们会假定虐待事件（再次重申，无论是否真实地记得）是导致他们当前心理状态的原因。但是，正如我们所看到的，这个结论可能是错误的。讽刺的是，通过证实性偏差，这个结论会强化一个人对此记忆的信念。
p156.en: What contribution does it make to the debate about “restored memories” after the fallacy of attribution? When people “recall” their memories and find that their memory of abuse (unsure or inaccurate) appears to be related to their current unhappiness, they assume that the abuse (repeated again, whether true or not) is the cause of their current psychological state. But, as we have seen, this conclusion may be wrong. Ironically, this conclusion strengthens one's belief in this memory by proving a sexual deviation.

p157.original: 我们能够得出什么结论？

p158.original: 那么，上述内容给了我们什么启示？请你使用具体问题具体分析的方式来衡量上述证据，并注意情绪偏差可能会对你的思维产生的影响。同时，也要记住以下几点。
p158.en: So, what does that tell us? Please use a specific analysis of the specific issues to measure the above evidence and to be mindful of the possible impact of emotional bias on your thinking. At the same time, the following points should also be borne in mind.

p159.original: 一方面，确实存在儿童性虐待事件，而且这种事件的发生会比上一代大多数专家所推测的更为普遍（McAnulty & Burnette，2004）。
p159.en: On the one hand, child sexual abuse does occur and can occur more widely than most experts in the previous generation have assumed (McAnulty & Burnette, 2004).

p160.original: 另一方面，那些由治疗师或警察的暗示引导回想起来的记忆特别容易被扭曲和捏造（Loftus，2003a）。因此，在没有独立证据的情况下，我们没有办法判断一个被恢复的记忆是真实的还是虚假的。
p160.en: On the other hand, memories that are inspired by the suggestion of the therapist or the police are particularly susceptible to distortion and fabrication (Loftus, 2003a). Therefore, without independent evidence, we cannot judge whether a restored memory is real or false.

p161.original: 请牢记，人们对虚假记忆的确定程度与他们对真实记忆的确定程度相同。
p161.en: Please bear in mind that false memories are determined to the same extent as their true memories.

p162.original: 尽管创伤性事件可以被遗忘，并在之后可以被回忆起来。但它们更有可能形成人们无法忘记的持久和侵入性的记忆。不过，像罗斯这样的案例告诉我们，关于被虐待的记忆的恢复可能是准确的。
p162.en: Although traumatic events can be forgotten and then recalled. But they are more likely to create lasting and intrusive memories that people cannot forget. However, cases such as Ross have shown us that the restoration of memory of ill-treatment may be accurate.

p163.original: 早期记忆，尤其是那些可能发生在婴儿期的事件，很可能只是人们的幻想或错误归因。正如我们所看到的，人们在3岁之前极少会形成对事件的情景记忆（Schacter，1996）。
p163.en: Early memories, especially those that may have occurred in infancy, are likely to be simply the illusions or the faulty attributions of people. As we have seen, the scenario memory of events is rarely formed before the age of three (Schacter, 1996).

p164.original: 比起那些声称一直在意识中存在的记忆，人们更应该对那些声称被“压抑”并在数年后“恢复”的记忆表示怀疑。
p164.en: The memories that claim to have been in consciousness should be more sceptical than those that claim to have been “pressed” and “recovered” several years later.
